findings.title: Hook fees not proportionally adjusted on partial fill, causing user overcharge
confidence_deductions: -10: requires partial fill (pool hits sqrtPrice limit)
-10: hook fees must be configured on the token (AMMStandardHook supports this natively)
-15: prior round R6 dismissed as by-design, but missed the asymmetry with exchange fee adjustment
findings.description: In _poolSwapByOutput and _poolSwapByInput, hook fees are stored via _storeHookFees BEFORE the pool call. On partial fill, exchange fees and LP fees are proportionally reduced (lines 1415-1426 for input, lines 1569-1583 for output), but stored hook fees are NOT adjusted. This creates a disproportionate fee charge: the hook receives the full fee while the pool only consumed a fraction of the swap amount. The user absorbs the overcharge as reduced output (output swaps) or increased cost (input swaps).
findings.impact: User overpays hook fees on partial fills. For 10% hook fee and 50% partial fill: user loses ~5% of their swap value to the hook compared to proportional allocation. Token creator (hook fee recipient) profits.
findings.proof_sketch: Numerical trace: Output swap requesting 1000 tokens, 10% hook fee. _applySwapByOutputOutputFees stores 100 tokens as hook fee, inflates amountOut to 1100. Pool partial fills to 550. amountOutAdjustment=550, adjustedAmountSpecified=1000-550=450. User gets 450. Hook gets full 100. Proportionally correct: user should get 500, hook 50. User loses 50 tokens (5%).
findings.victim: Swap users who experience partial fills on pools with token hook fees
findings.extractable_value: hookFeeBPS * (originalAmount - actualAmount) / MAX_BPS per partial fill swap. For 500 BPS (5%) hook fee on 100 ETH swap with 50% fill: ~2.5 ETH overcharge.
attack_sequence: 1. Token creator configures hook fees via CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.setTokenSettings (e.g., 500 BPS sell fee)
2. User initiates output-based swap requesting X output tokens
3. AMMModule._executeBeforeSwapHooks computes hook fee F = hookBPS * X / MAX_BPS
4. _applySwapByOutputOutputFees stores F in tokensOwed and inflates amountOut to X + F
5. Pool type hits sqrtPriceLimit, returns actualAmountOut < X + F (partial fill)
6. Partial fill adjustment reduces adjustedAmountSpecified but does NOT reduce stored hook fee F
7. User receives adjustedAmountSpecified (reduced) while hook claims full F
8. Hook fee recipient (token creator) collects overcharge via collectHookFeesByHook
prerequisites: Token must have hook fees configured (AMMStandardHook supports natively)
Swap must hit sqrtPriceLimit causing partial fill (normal market condition)

kill_gate.reason: Exchange fees ARE adjusted (lines 1420-1426) but hook fees are NOT — asymmetry is clear. Refutation: this could be intentional if hook fees are designed to be non-refundable commitments. Counter-refutation: exchange fees and LP fees are proportionally adjusted, but hook fees are not. No code comment explains this inconsistency.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-01: Non-token hook fee key mismatch (_storeNonTokenHookFees vs _transferHookFeesByHook)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Keys match when tokenFor == tokenFee (the standard case). _storeNonTokenHookFees uses hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFor)) while _transferHookFeesByHook uses hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). Mismatch only when hook uses cross-token fee collection, which is an API footgun but not exploitable with AMMStandardHook. Forge test proves keys match for same-token case and mismatch for cross-token case.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-03: 100% fee asymmetry (input allows 10000 BPS, output rejects)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Intentional design documented in CODEBASE_MAP. At AMMModule.sol:1717, input swaps use > (allows 10000) while output swaps use >= (rejects 10000). This prevents division by zero on output. User protected by limitAmount check at line 2156. A 100% fee on input yields 0 output; limitAmount > 0 would revert. Requires compromised pool hook (Tier C).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-04: Reentrancy during queued hook fee distribution via ERC-777 callback
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers has self-call guard at ModuleFeeCollection.sol:128 (msg.sender != address(this)). CLOB uses separate TstorishReentrancyGuard. Even if AMM reentrancy flags cleared at line 3190, CLOB's own nonReentrant blocks re-entry into CLOB functions. Forge test proves external call reverts from both attacker and admin addresses.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-05: feeOnTop extraction on partial fill permits
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop is NOT signed in SWAP_TYPEHASH but user's limitAmount caps total input cost. For output swaps: amountIn (includes feeOnTop) <= limitAmount at line 2171. For input swaps: feeOnTop deducted from input reduces output, checked against limitAmount at line 2156. Forge test proves mathematically that extraction is bounded by limitAmount gap. Documented as intentional design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-07: afterSwapRefund DoS via reentrancy consuming CLOB deposits
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB's ammHandleTransfer, depositToken, openOrder, closeOrder all use nonReentrant (TstorishReentrancyGuard). Even if AMM reentrancy flags cleared during fee distribution at line 3190, CLOB's own guard blocks re-entry. afterSwapRefund requires msg.sender == AMM (line 316). Forge test proves external calls revert from both attacker and admin.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-08: Hook fees amplify minimum protocol fee (hop fee shortage)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Intentional design. Hop fees are protocol revenue guarantee. At AMMModule.sol:2652, when protocolFeeFromHookFees + expectedProtocolLPFee < minimumProtocolFee, a shortage is computed and extracted from input. High hook fees reduce LP fee base, making shortage more likely. Forge test reproduces exact math: 1000 input with 50% hook fee, 5% hop fee → shortage = 24.5, protocolFeeFromInput ≈ 24.52. Total protocol fee reaches designed minimum of 50. User's limitAmount protects against unexpected costs.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-09: Fill-or-kill permits revert with any input fee
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hypothesis was wrong about the data flow. In _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse at line 2160: amountIn = adjustedAmountSpecified = ORIGINAL amount (not reduced by fees). For input-based FOK: handler receives full adjustedAmountSpecified = amountSpecified. FOK check: uint256(amountSpecified) != amountIn → 1000 != 1000 → FALSE → passes. Fees are deducted from swapCache.amountIn (pool amount) but the TOTAL collection amount is preserved. Forge test proves math.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-10: Multi-hop insufficient output after hook fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Derivative of H-08. Each hop's output becomes next hop's input. Protocol fee enforcement per hop is independent. Forge test models 3-hop cascade: 1000 input with 30% hook fee on hop 1 → 693 → 686 → 679 output. Without hook fees: 970. Ratio ≈ 70%, matching the 30% hook fee impact. User's limitAmount on final output protects against unexpected total slippage.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-11: CLOB stale pricing bounds after registryUpdatePricingBounds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By design. _enforceTokenHooks validates bounds at openOrder (CLOBTransferHandler.sol:534) but not at fillOrder (line 275). Orders are maker commitments at specific prices. Retroactive bound changes would break maker expectations. The executor (taker) CHOOSES which orders to fill — no rational executor fills at worse-than-market prices. Forge test verifies full CLOB lifecycle including access control (wrong maker rejected).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R7-CH-12: CLOB double rounding accumulation in calculateFixedInput
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: calculateFixedInput uses 2x mulDivRoundingUp (CLOBHelper.sol:313-314): max 2 wei rounding per order fill. Over 200 orders: max 400 wei total overpayment. At ETH=$3000: 400 wei = $0.0000000000000012 — far below any submission threshold. Forge test verifies across 5 input amounts × 4 prices that error is always ≤ 2 wei per calculation and rounding consistently favors maker.

theft_theses.thesis: Token creator extracts excess hook fees from users via partial fill overcharge
theft_theses.asset: Output tokens (output swaps) or excess input tokens (input swaps)

theft_theses.thesis: Executor extracts feeOnTop from permit users beyond signed limits
Attacker replays permit signatures for double-spend
Attacker drains CLOB deposits via wrong-maker closeOrder
Reentrancy during hook fee distribution steals CLOB maker funds
Non-token hook fee key mismatch causes permanent fee loss
Fill-or-kill permits broken by fee deduction (permanent DoS)
CLOB stale pricing bounds enable off-market fills
CLOB rounding accumulation drains pool over many fills
100% fee asymmetry enables pool drain via compromised hook
Hook fee + minimum protocol fee amplification extracts user value

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a custom hook developer called collectHookFeesByHook(token0, token1, ...) expecting to collect fees 'associated with token0 paid in token1', the lookup key hash(hook, hash(token0, token1)) would NOT match the storage key hash(hook, hash(token0, token0)) used by _storeNonTokenHookFees, permanently locking the fees.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:3018 — _storeNonTokenHookFees uses tokenFor TWICE. No guard prevents mismatch; retrieval requires caller to know the correct key pattern (tokenFor == tokenFee).
hypothesis_results.detail: API footgun for custom hooks, not exploitable with AMMStandardHook. Keys match when tokenFor == tokenFee (standard case). Forge test proves key computation: storeKey == retrieveKey when same tokens, storeKey != retrieveKey when different tokens.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker controlled a pool hook and returned 10000 BPS (100%) for an input-based swap, the user loses their entire input amount because _getPoolFee at line 1717 uses > (not >=) for input swaps, allowing 10000 through.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:2156 — limitAmount check: if (swapCache.amountOut < swapOrder.limitAmount) revert. User with limitAmount > 0 would cause revert when output = 0 from 100% fee.
hypothesis_results.detail: Intentional design documented in CODEBASE_MAP. 100% input fee prevents division by zero on output. User protected by limitAmount. Requires compromised pool hook (Tier C) AND user sets limitAmount = 0. Forge test verifies: lpFee = amountIn when poolFeeBPS = 10000, amountAfterFee = 0, and limitAmount > 0 causes revert.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an ERC-777 token's transfer callback fired during executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers (after reentrancy flags cleared at line 3190), it could re-enter the AMM to create a nested swap whose hook fees would be lost when transient storage resets.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: ModuleFeeCollection.sol:128 — if (msg.sender != address(this)) revert LBAMM__CallerMustBeSelf. Additionally, CLOB uses TstorishReentrancyGuard (separate from AMM's diamond flags).
hypothesis_results.detail: Self-call guard + CLOB's separate TstorishReentrancyGuard block all attack paths. External call to executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers reverts. Even with AMM flags cleared, CLOB nonReentrant prevents re-entry into CLOB functions. Forge test confirms external calls revert from both attacker and admin.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an executor set feeOnTop to 99% of the swap amount, the user would receive near-zero tokens because feeOnTop is NOT signed in SWAP_TYPEHASH and the ratio check in _executePartialFillPermit uses amountOut (not net-of-feeOnTop).
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:2171 — if (swapCache.amountIn > swapOrder.limitAmount) revert LBAMM__LimitAmountExceeded. For output swaps, amountIn includes feeOnTop, so high feeOnTop causes amountIn to exceed limitAmount.
hypothesis_results.detail: limitAmount + ratio check protect user. For output swaps: max feeOnTop = limitAmount - poolCost - exchangeFee. Forge test proves: with limitAmount = 600, poolCost = 400, exchangeFee = 10, max extraction = 190. Tight limit of 415 caps extraction to 5. Documented intentional design.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If partial fill hook fee overcharge is by design, then exchange fees would also NOT be adjusted. But exchange fees ARE proportionally adjusted at lines 1420-1426, while hook fees are NOT — this asymmetry suggests a bug, not intentional behavior.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: NONE — no guard adjusts hook fees on partial fill. AMMModule.sol:1576 adjusts adjustedAmountSpecified but does not reduce stored hook fees at lines 2871/2887.
hypothesis_results.detail: CONFIRMED as AUTH-001. Hook fees stored at full amount even on partial fill. Numerical proof: 1000 output request, 10% hook fee → 100 stored. Pool partial fills to 550. User gets adjustedAmountSpecified = 450 instead of proportional 500. Overcharge = 50. Exchange fees ARE adjusted (lines 1420-1426) but hook fees are NOT — clear asymmetry.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a malicious hook fee recipient contract re-entered the AMM during fee distribution (after reentrancy flags cleared at line 3190), it could initiate a second CLOB swap that consumes the same maker-deposited tokens needed by afterSwapRefund.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: CLOBTransferHandler.sol:229 — nonReentrant modifier (TstorishReentrancyGuard). This is a SEPARATE guard from the AMM's diamond flags, so clearing AMM flags doesn't affect CLOB's protection.
hypothesis_results.detail: CLOB nonReentrant blocks all re-entry paths during fee distribution. afterSwapRefund also requires msg.sender == AMM (line 316). Forge test proves: external call to afterSwapRefund from attacker and admin both revert with CallbackMustBeFromAMM.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a token has 50% hook fees and 5% hop fee, the minimum protocol fee is computed on the ORIGINAL input (before hook fees), creating a shortage that forces additional protocolFeeFromInput extraction from the already-reduced swap amount, leaving far less for the actual swap than the user anticipated.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:2652 — shortage check IS the designed enforcement mechanism. There is no guard against it because hop fees are an intentional protocol revenue floor.
hypothesis_results.detail: Intentional design. Forge test reproduces exact math: 1000 input, 50% hook fee, 5% hop fee, 1% pool fee, 10% LP protocol fee → minimumProtocolFee = 50, protocolFeeFromHookFees = 25, expectedProtocolLPFee = 0.5, shortage = 24.5, protocolFeeFromInput ≈ 24.52. Total protocol fee reaches designed minimum of 50. Also verified: shortage triggers even without hook fees when hop fee is high (5% hop, 1% pool). This is the designed fee mechanism.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If amountIn passed to the handler differs from amountSpecified due to fee deductions, the FOK check uint256(swapOrder.amountSpecified) != amountIn would fire and revert, making FOK permits incompatible with any exchange fee.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:2160 — swapCache.amountIn = swapCache.adjustedAmountSpecified. The TOTAL collection amount (including fees) is preserved, not the post-fee amount.
hypothesis_results.detail: Hypothesis was wrong about data flow. adjustedAmountSpecified preserves the TOTAL collection amount. For input-based FOK: handler receives adjustedAmountSpecified = original amountSpecified = 1000. FOK check: 1000 != 1000 → false → passes. Fees are deducted from swapCache.amountIn (pool amount) internally, but the handler sees the total. Forge test proves the math.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: In a 3-hop swap with high hook fees on the first hop and hop fees on each hop, the fee cascade could reduce the amount reaching later hops so severely that the last hop's reserve update underflows.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:2156 — limitAmount check on FINAL output protects user. Each hop is independently validated. Pool types handle insufficient liquidity gracefully (partial fill or revert).
hypothesis_results.detail: Derivative of H-08. Forge test models 3-hop cascade: 1000 input, 30% hook fee on hop 1, 1% pool fee per hop → output ≈ 679. Without hook fees: output ≈ 970. Ratio ≈ 70%, exactly matching the 30% hook fee impact. Fee cascading is mathematically predictable and user's limitAmount on final output provides protection.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a token creator tightens pricing bounds after CLOB orders are placed, existing orders execute at prices outside the new bounds, allowing makers to have their orders filled at extreme prices that the creator intended to prohibit.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: CLOBTransferHandler.sol:534 — _enforceTokenHooks called in openOrder validates bounds. Line 275: ammHandleTransfer calls fillOrder with NO pricing bounds re-check.
hypothesis_results.detail: By design. CLOB orders are maker commitments at specific prices. Executor (taker) CHOOSES which orders to fill — no rational executor fills at worse-than-market prices. Retroactive bound changes would break maker expectations. Forge test verifies full CLOB lifecycle: deposit → open → close → withdraw with proper access control (wrong maker rejected).

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker places many minimum-sized orders at sequential price ticks, the two mulDivRoundingUp operations accumulate 0-2 wei per fill step, extracting a measurable maker surplus at the executor's expense over hundreds of fills.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: CLOBHelper.sol:313-314 — mulDivRoundingUp is standard math. Rounding UP favors maker (output side), which is the conventional direction in AMMs.
hypothesis_results.detail: Max 2 wei per fill, dust level. Forge test verifies across 5 inputs × 4 prices: error always ≤ 2 wei per calculation. Over 200 fills: max 400 wei = $0.0000000000000012 at ETH=$3000. Rounding consistently favors maker (tested across 100 sequential amounts). Well below any submission threshold.
